framework_findings: EXPERT-mode strided GM box writes are first-class: `T.copy(ub, Output[bz, row0:row0+half, hq, :])` against a 4-D BSND declaration lowers to ONE tl::ascend::copy_ub_to_gm<T,D,half>/DataCopyPad with DataCopyExtParams(blockCount=half, blockLen=D*sizeof(T), dstStride=(N_q*D-D)*sizeof(T)) — the instruction count is IDENTICAL to the contiguous form (measured: 65/81/105/209 both arms), only dstStride differs. Measured strided/contiguous MTE3 time ratio per 8KB box: 1.07-1.17 (probe_iter8_P2_bsnd.py, 16 msprof dirs).

The 2-D flattened form (Output declared [B*S, N_q*D], box = (bz*S+row0:+half, hq*D:+D)) is FUNCTIONALLY bit-exact too but emits a runtime row-count CLAMP conditional in the descriptor position (extra scalar work + the iter2 'condval in an expression position' hazard) — prefer the 4-D declaration with a unit-extent head dim.

torch.equal is NOT a bit-identity test on NaN-carrying tensors: it uses IEEE == so every NaN position reports a difference even when the payloads are byte-identical (measured: all differing positions hold 0x7fff in BOTH arms, and BASE-vs-BASE re-runs show the same artifact). Use t.view(torch.int16) equality for bit-identity when special values are injected.

A CPU-fp32 golden with atol=1e-3 mis-flags shipped bf16 shapes (r3: viol=12 at max_diff 3.2e-3). test_gqa.py's f6-verified policy (golden in the input dtype on NPU, atol 1e-3 fp16 / 2e-2 bf16, rtol 1e-2) gives viol=0. Gate harnesses should compare viol_arm == viol_base as well, so a precision change in either direction cannot slip through.

Eliminating an aux kernel can make the MAIN kernel faster, not slower: 4 of 5 covered shapes measured main TaskDur -0.07%..-1.00% with the strided write, because the output tensor is no longer written BHSD and then re-read by transpose_out (one less L2 write+read pass). The naive 'strided write must cost more' model over-predicts the net effect.

A capability flag on the returned closure (`_run.out_bsnd = bsnd_eff and chosen in _P2_BSND_KERNELS`) is the safe way to let an adapter skip a post-processing kernel: it is derived from the RESOLVED spec, so a compile fallback down the chain automatically reverts to the old path instead of silently returning the wrong layout. The layout flag must also enter the build cache key (chain_key) or a factory caller and the adapter can share one cached chain with incompatible layouts.

Cross-session variance on launch-floor-dominated micro-kernels is ~+-10%: the r1 transpose_out (0.5MB, blk=16) measured 4.86us (iter7 A/B) / 5.20us (iter7 Gate 3, same file) / 4.80-5.62us within this session / 5.49us (this session's decision samples). Anchor bands for such components need a wider tolerance than the +-3% used for >=20us kernels.
antipattern_check: performance-antipatterns.md re-checked against the new code. (1) 'launch core 数需要重点关注': P2 REMOVES a kernel launch per call on the covered domain (transpose_out) and removes nothing else — strictly positive. The one intentionally RETAINED item is unchanged and documented since iter1 §7.2: the per-head AUTO ladder launches by block_num (关注项 A) — it is the D!=128 / instance-short fallback path, Fixed-Core-izing it equals a kernel rewrite, and its benefit surface is narrow. (2) 'tile size 过小导致片上内存浪费': the FIN box stays [half=32, D=128] and the UB/L1/L0/ws footprint is byte-identical (0 new bytes, audited); the GM write's burst granularity (32 x 256B) is what transpose_out has always used in production and what the decode BSND path uses — measured cost 1.07-1.17x per box, and four of five covered shapes got marginally FASTER overall because the L2 no longer absorbs an extra write+read pass of the output tensor. (3) '纯 AIV memory bound 算子未做流水/双 buffer': the fix applied is the strongest form — the pure-AIV memory-bound kernel is eliminated outright on 7/20 bench cases. (4) '冗余全局同步': no sync/flag/sem line changed (byte-identical, asserted by the generator). (5) AIC/AIV workspace & L2 guidance: L2 traffic drops by one full output read+write pass per call (e.g. r4: -32MB). No new violations.
